verdict.rationale: Homebrew installs each package into its own keg inside a single shared Cellar and symlinks it into the prefix. That gives a global, machine-wide store, so one installed version serves every project that relies on it, including Brewfile-based projects. Nothing in the evidence shows this store is content-addressable: kegs are organized by package, not by content hash. Missing for 10: content-addressable (hash-keyed) storage, documented deduplication guarantees, per-project version isolation backed by a shared store, independent corroboration of disk-space savings.
